{
  "strategy": "increase_compute_units_to_16384",
  "hardware_update": {
    "num_chiplets": 16,
    "compute_units": 16384,
    "buffer_size": 8192,
    "system_params": {"dram_bw": 64, "nop_bw": 128, "micro_batch": 2, "tensor_parall": 16},
    "chiplet_type": "ws"
  },
  "selected_hardware_candidate": "modify_hardware_parameter_771e71e98c62f9f4",
  "actions": [
    "chiplets.compute_units: {'4096': 16}->{'16384': 16}",
    "chiplets.macs: {'[8,8,8,8]': 16}->{'[8,8,16,16]': 16}"
  ],
  "rationale": "The bottleneck state shows purely compute-bound FFN1 tilings (99.99% compute time, 98.4% compute energy) with 4096 compute units per WS chiplet. Each of the 16 FFN1 tilings consumes ~14.5B latency on its assigned chiplet via tensor_parall=16. Increasing compute_units from 4096 to 16384 reduces FFN1 latency by ~4x (to ~3.6B per tiling), cutting critical path latency from ~29.1B to ~18.2B. Compute energy scales proportionally with compute time, so energy also decreases significantly. Although monetary cost will increase (compute cost is 49.3% of total), the combined latency-energy reduction is substantial enough to plausibly compensate. No historical cases exist to contradict this direction. The candidate was materialized via modify_hardware_parameter and is ready for evaluation.",
  "notes": {
    "history_usage": "No retrieved historical cases were available. The decision is based solely on the bottleneck evidence and design-space analysis.",
    "cost_risk": "Monetary cost is expected to increase because compute cost (49.3% of total) scales with compute_units. However, the ~4x latency reduction and proportional energy reduction for the dominant FFN1 layers should offset the cost increase, improving the combined objective.",
    "expected_objective_direction": "decrease",
    "rejected_alternatives": [
      "Increasing num_chiplets to 32: would increase monetary cost significantly (more chiplets, more compute) without directly addressing the per-chiplet compute bottleneck; the FFN1 tilings would still be compute-bound on each chiplet.",
      "Increasing tensor_parall to 32: would require more chiplets or finer tiling, increasing communication overhead and monetary cost without addressing the per-chiplet compute deficiency.",
      "Switching to OS chiplet type: OS dataflow may not improve compute-bound GEMMs and could increase NoP pressure and monetary cost.",
      "Increasing buffer_size: the bottleneck is compute, not buffer capacity; buffer_size increase would add cost without reducing FFN1 latency.",
      "Increasing dram_bw or nop_bw: the bottleneck is compute (99.99%), not memory or communication bandwidth; these would add cost without benefit."
    ],
    "risk": "The main risk is that the monetary cost increase from 4x compute units may be larger than anticipated, potentially offsetting the latency-energy gains. However, given the extreme compute dominance (99.99% of FFN1 time), the latency reduction is highly predictable, and the energy reduction is proportional, making this a low-risk high-reward move."
  }
}
